items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1959-07-16
items.q: So right away we got on the phone, we got ahold of Freddie Newman. And, uh, Freddie come up... Before we could, the only one that he knew out of, uh, out of the four of them was High Society. And we had, we had to teach him the tunes.

ctx.x: Five pennies and all, yeah. With the pennies.

He used to call it, used to call it futuristic, instead of calling it progressive or modern like they call it now, they used to call it futuristic music. And if you play it that way, you know, you, uh, you ahead of time. Used to try to, 된 stuff with stuff with stuff with stuff with stuff with stuff with stuff stuff with stuff with stuff

It involved arrangements and all kind of interludes and things like that. Sidney Arden was hella on that. He always had to have a cadenza at the end of the tune, you know. It's a funny story, Bill, when we were making those recordings. We had one of those tunes there. We get to the end of it and there's a clarinet cadenza. Well, when we made them, I had an infected toe, so I was using a stick. See, in a shoe, open shoe like this. And I had one of those big Chinese gongs, you know. So I had to hit one lick before…
